scenes.title: Examiner's Margin / Household Expenditure
scenes.narration: Welcome to IELTS Winners and Examiner's Margin. We are learning to analyse a table of household expenditure and write a high-scoring four-paragraph Task One response. Notice the four countries: Canada, Japan, Mexico, and Germany. The table compares housing, food, transport, and other expenses. Our aim is to identify the key figures, write a useful overview, and make accurate comparisons, rather than listing every percentage.

scenes.title: Step 3 / Language Toolkit
scenes.narration: Now let's strengthen the language of the report. A figure of forty-eight percent is nearly half. Twenty-eight percent is slightly over a quarter, twenty-four percent is almost a quarter, twenty percent is one fifth, and ten percent is one tenth. We can vary the verbs too: account for, make up, comprise, and represent. Use phrases such as whereas, in contrast, and similarly to connect meaningful comparisons. Remember that an overview should describe the main pattern without becoming a list of figures.

scenes.title: Steps 4 to 7 / Grouping, Upgrading and Strategy
scenes.narration: This slide shows how to group and improve the data. First, group related categories, such as housing and food, and compare those figures. Then compare the smaller or contrasting categories, especially transport and others. Upgrade simple sentences by explaining which country has the highest share, and by making clear comparisons. Avoid three common mistakes: copying the given introduction, repeating figures in the overview, and comparing without a clear point. The final structure is simple: introduction, overview, body paragraph one, and body paragraph two.

scenes.title: Step 2 / Four-Paragraph Response
scenes.narration: Here is the writing plan in action. Paragraph one paraphrases what the table shows. Paragraph two provides the overview, focusing on the biggest patterns rather than listing numbers. Paragraph three compares the higher figures, while paragraph four covers the remaining categories. In the model response, look at how each paragraph has a specific purpose. Use percentages only where they support a comparison. The takeaway is clear: the overview gives the main trends, and the body paragraphs give the supporting evidence.

scenes.title: Step 1 / Analyse the Table
scenes.narration: Finally, here is the analysis checklist behind a strong response. Use E R C S: Extremes, Rankings, Comparisons, and Spread. Extremes means finding the highest and lowest values. Rankings show which category leads in each country. Comparisons identify similarities and differences, while spread shows how much the figures vary. For example, others reaches forty-eight percent in Japan, whereas transport falls to ten percent there. This checklist helps you choose the most important data before you write. Follow these steps, and your table response will be clearer and more focused.
